description: Architectural rules for distributed services, service boundaries, resilient communication, and event-driven data consistency.

rules.name: Database-per-Service Isolation
rules.description: Prohibits microservices from directly accessing, querying, or mutating the database or schema belonging to another microservice.
rules.rationale: Direct database sharing creates tight coupling, breaks service autonomy, prevents independent deployments, and introduces distributed schema lock-in.
rules.remediation: Communicate exclusively via well-defined public APIs (gRPC / REST) or asynchronous domain events over message brokers (Kafka / RabbitMQ).

rules.name: Mandatory Distributed Tracing & Correlation ID Propagation
rules.description: All inbound and outbound HTTP requests, gRPC calls, and messaging events must extract and propagate a standard Correlation ID / Trace Context header (e.g., X-Correlation-ID or traceparent).
rules.rationale: Distributed tracing is essential for troubleshooting cross-service latency, cascaded failures, and debugging production workflows.
rules.remediation: Inject correlation ID middleware to attach trace context to loggers and all outbound HTTP/gRPC/event clients.

rules.name: Resilient Inter-Service Calls (Timeout & Circuit Breaker)
rules.description: Synchronous HTTP/gRPC inter-service clients must configure explicit connection/read timeouts and circuit breaker/fallback mechanisms.
rules.rationale: Prevents thread pool exhaustion, cascading outages, and catastrophic backpressure when a downstream dependency is degraded or unreachable.
rules.remediation: Wrap external HTTP/gRPC calls with resilience policies (e.g., Polly, Resilience4j, or custom timeout/retry wrappers).

rules.name: Transactional Outbox Pattern for State-Event Consistency
rules.description: Prohibits publishing message broker events directly inside an uncommitted database transaction or without dual-write transactional consistency.
rules.rationale: Avoids phantom event publication if the database transaction rolls back, or lost events if the message broker is unreachable.
rules.remediation: Persist the domain event to an Outbox table within the same ACID transaction and publish asynchronously via an Outbox worker/relay.

rules.name: Idempotent Event Consumers
rules.description: Event handlers and message consumers must implement idempotency checks to safely handle duplicate message delivery.
rules.rationale: Distributed message brokers guarantee at-least-once delivery; consumers must remain robust against redeliveries and rebalancing.
rules.remediation: Track processed message IDs in a deduplication store or design state transitions to be naturally idempotent.
